source_name: Trade magazin - OKSZ tag feed (retail trade media)
why_relevant: FMCG/retail trade magazine with a standing tag for OKSZ; captures merchant-association statements on payment acceptance, cash mandates and checkout technology that do not always reach oksz.hu, and points to further retail-side actors.

source_name: Wikipédia (hu) entries for Magyar Bankszövetség and Országos Kereskedelmi Szövetség
why_relevant: Low-credibility but high-yield orientation layer: gives founding dates (Bankszövetség registered Feb 1989; OKSZ founded 23 Apr 1990), officeholders, alias names and outbound links used to seed further searches. Never cite as evidence; use for glossary and entity resolution only.

source_name: Visa Magyarország – Visa szerkesztőség / sajtóközlemények
why_relevant: Visa's Hungarian press room publishes HU-specific consumer payment research, contactless/tokenised transaction growth figures and e-commerce behaviour stats, typically earlier and with more marketing granularity than MNB statistics. Individual releases carry percentages on contactless penetration, mobile wallet share and online purchase security attitudes.

source_name: Mastercard Newsroom Europe – Hungarian press releases
why_relevant: Mastercard's HU newsroom is the publication channel for the long-running 'Bankkártya Használati Szokások és Attitűdök' survey (15+ annual waves) plus acceptance-network releases (e.g. terminal growth, Doppio programme). Provides card penetration, mobile payment adoption and acceptance-point counts that predate or complement MNB data.

source_name: Mastercard Digitális Fizetési Index (Hungary landing page)
source_subtype: scheme index / recurring study landing page
why_relevant: Recurring composite index measuring digitalisation of Hungarian payments; a repeatable time-series indicator published by a scheme rather than a regulator, useful for triangulating cash-displacement trends.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide Investor Relations – quarterly results & SEC filings (EFT Processing segment)
why_relevant: Parent-company filings disclose installed ATM counts and growth by segment/region and transaction volumes. 10-K/10-Q/8-K are audited or CFO-signed, giving a legally-backed baseline for Euronet's European ATM estate that can be cross-checked against HU-level claims.

source_name: Global Payments Magyarország (globalpayments.com/hu-hu)
why_relevant: Major HU acquirer/terminal operator (took over Erste Bank's POS estate in 2014; participant in Mastercard's Doppio acceptance-expansion programme). HU site and product pages reveal terminal portfolio, softPOS offering and occasionally merchant/terminal counts; the company profile also anchors an entity for company-register cross-checks.

source_name: Worldline Magyarország (worldline.com/hu-hu)
why_relevant: Worldline Financial Services is one of the largest bank-independent card acceptance providers active in HU (post SIX Payment Services / Six-Payment heritage), distributing via partners such as Bizpay. HU pages document terminal ranges, wallet acceptance and webshop plugin coverage — useful for acceptance-technology diffusion tracking.

source_name: Bizpay (Worldline hivatalos magyarországi partner)
why_relevant: Reseller/distribution partner for Worldline in Hungary; its FAQ and pricing pages expose merchant-facing fee structures, terminal types and integration coverage that the principal does not publish locally — a proxy for acceptance-market pricing and competitive positioning.

source_name: Nexi Central Europe / Nexi Hungary Zrt.
why_relevant: Nexi Group entered the Hungarian market via Nexi Central Europe (and a registered Nexi Hungary Zrt. / Nexi Central Europe a.s. Magyarországi Fióktelepe). Activity covers full issuing+acquiring processing and terminal management — a new structural actor in HU card processing whose entry/market-share moves are worth tracking.

source_name: Cardnet Zrt. (POS terminal service, cash registers, loyalty/gift cards)
why_relevant: Long-standing Hungarian POS terminal service / cash-register and card-personalisation company; relevant as a terminal-estate service actor. Only a LinkedIn company page was confirmed in search — its own corporate domain was not established in this pass, so the LinkedIn profile is the confirmed pointer.

source_name: OTP Bank kártyaelfogadás (acquiring) product pages
why_relevant: Largest HU bank acquirer's merchant-facing pages document POS terminal offers, subsidy schemes and acceptance solutions; changes in offer structure signal acceptance-network expansion drivers (e.g. state POS-installation subsidy).

source_name: K&H Pénzforgalmi Szolgáltató Kft. (khpos.hu) – bank-affiliated acquirer
why_relevant: Dedicated acquiring subsidiary of K&H (KBC) with its own merchant portal; one of the four principal bank acquirers in HU alongside OTP, Erste (via Global Payments) and MBH. Useful for terminal product/pricing tracking and as an entity for register-based financials.

source_name: MBH Bank – POS elfogadás
why_relevant: Third large HU banking group (post Budapest Bank / MKB / Takarék merger) offering card acceptance; tracks consolidation effects on the acquiring landscape and terminal offers.

source_name: Barion Payment Zrt. – corporate site, pricing and customer-service knowledge base
why_relevant: Hungarian-developed e-money institution and second-largest HU online PSP (~20-25% of the PSP market per trade commentary). Unlike SimplePay it publishes a public price list (transaction fees ~0.5-1.5%), making it the best public benchmark for HU online acceptance pricing; also publishes product/statistics features (Barion Pixel) and periodic commercial communications.

source_name: Fizetési Pont (OFSZ) – softPOS / POS terminal operator
why_relevant: Self-described third-largest POS terminal operator in Hungary and first HU softPOS deployer (inside Mastercard's Doppio programme); the sole provider channelling the Ministry of Finance's HUF 80,000 non-refundable POS-installation subsidy. Its blog/press output is the closest thing to public data on subsidised terminal rollout volumes.

source_name: Fintech.hu / FinTechRadar.hu – HU payments trade news
why_relevant: Secondary HU fintech outlets carrying scheme and PSP announcements (e.g. Visa digital payment programme launches, SimplePay restructuring). Useful redundancy when a corporate newsroom drops or reorganises URLs.

source_name: PosNavigator.eu – HU POS provider comparison portal
why_relevant: Comparison portal enumerating HU POS terminal providers with pricing and feature matrices — a shortcut to a near-complete actor list of terminal operators serving HU merchants, including smaller players not visible in scheme communications.

source_name: MagNet Bank – ATM network transition notices (Euronet outsourcing)
why_relevant: Bank-side notices about handing ATM estates to Euronet reveal outsourcing deals and effective network sizes ('over 500 Euronet ATMs available to customers') that neither party announces as a headline statistic — an indirect but datable indicator of ATM-estate consolidation in Hungary.

source_name: Consumer/comparison sites tracking ATM fees and network size (Wise HU blog, Biztosdöntés)
why_relevant: These pages track independent-ATM surcharge levels and network descriptions over time; surcharge structure is a leading indicator of IAD economics and of cash-access cost in Hungary, which is not published by the operators themselves.

source_name: Mainstream HU business media covering ATM/POS network numbers (Origo, Pénzcentrum, HVG, Portfolio, Forbes.hu)
why_relevant: General business media report ATM-per-settlement rollout programmes and terminal-count milestones, often quoting operators or the ministry before any structured dataset is published. HVG/Forbes also host acquirer brand-content that leaks operational detail (e.g. Global Payments softPOS, Doppio targets).

source_name: E-commerce platform / integrator comparison content on HU PSPs (Shoptet blog, eClick, WeboldalSzeged, Zunapro)
why_relevant: Platform and agency comparisons are the only public source venturing HU PSP market-share estimates (SimplePay ~60-65%, Barion ~20-25%) and up-to-date fee ranges, plus they surface newer entrants (ShoptetPay, Stripe, Paylike) that scheme communications ignore.

source_name: OTP Bank Nyrt. – Éves jelentés (integrált éves jelentés) landing page
why_relevant: Hub for OTP's integrated annual reports, which carry Hungarian-operation business volumes: card portfolio counts (bankkártya darabszám), ATM and branch network size, POS/merchant acquiring context and digital channel usage. OTP is the largest HU issuer/acquirer, so its own disclosure is the single richest private-ecosystem datapoint.

source_name: OTP Bank Nyrt. – Jelentések (quarterly/flash reports index)
why_relevant: Quarterly flash reports and interim management reports give higher-frequency (quarterly) series on Hungarian retail volumes, digital customer counts and transactional trends — the only quarterly cadence available from a private HU issuer.

source_name: OTP Group Investor Relations (otpgroup.info) – reports & presentations
why_relevant: English-language IR portal of OTP Group carrying analyst presentations and report archives; presentations are where digital KPIs (digitally active clients, mobile app users, card spend growth) are visualised per country including Hungary.

source_name: MBH Bank Nyrt. – negyedéves gyorsjelentések és befektetői prezentációk (static file store)
source_subtype: bank IR / quarterly report + investor day deck
why_relevant: MBH (merged MKB+Takarék+Budapest Bank) is the #2 HU banking group; its quarterly reports and Investor Day decks contain retail customer counts, digital/mobile penetration and card portfolio commentary. Investor Day deck (Oct 2025) observed as a live PDF.

source_name: MBH Bank sajtószoba (press room)
why_relevant: Press releases disclose payment-product metrics that never reach the annual report — e.g. SZÉP-card digitalisation, mobile wallet tokenisation growth multiples, transaction share shifts. Useful as a leading indicator for wallet adoption.
